SYDNEY, Oct 16 : Australia coach Les Kiss is confident Mark Nawaqanitawase will return to the Wallabies after his two-year stint in rugby league but warned the athletic winger would have to earn his spot in the team.  Nawaqanitawase finished up his spell with the Sydney Roosters after his tries helped them to the National Rugby League (NRL) title earlier this month and is returning to the 15-man game on a two-year deal with Japan's Wild Knights.  The 26-year-old's agent Milan Volavola-Shankar said on Tuesday that there was no guarantee Nawaqanitawase would play for the Wallabies again given he would also qualify to play for Fiji or Italy from midway through next year.  Kiss said he accepted that Nawaqanitawase would not be available for November's Nations Championship games in Europe but thought he would be back in the green and gold of Australia before next year's World Cup on home soil.

"We've had a couple of chats and (we were) always waiting for the end of the year to see where he sits," Kiss told reporters on Thursday after naming his team for this weekend's clash with the All Blacks.   "He's had a big year, a fantastic year, hasn't he? So the conversations are being wrapped around making sure we get what's right for him. "I think there's no doubt that you know he wants to be back in the game for us, that's for sure," Kiss added.  "So we'll continue our conversations and go from there. I'm not going to speak on his behalf. That's all. But we know where he wants to play." Kiss, himself a former rugby league winger, said Nawaqanitawase would need some time to readjust to rugby union and was not certain to come straight back into the Australia side.  "Everyone will earn their way," he said. "But if he's playing good footy, he'll be in the mix, that's for sure. There's no doubt he's a quality player that we'll keep an eye on.  "He'll have some opportunities but first and foremost, (he needs to) get his rest, get himself together and get into some rugby back in Japan.  "It's a different game in terms of height and how you attack the game, how you move in the game, how you defend, how the aerial game is different, so he's got a lot of things just to relearn.  "Won't take him long, that's for sure." Nawaqanitawase made 11 appearances for the Wallabies before switching to the NRL, where he built a reputation as one of the game's biggest aerial threats as well as someone able to conjure up stunning tries.

Source: Reuters

FAST

BANGKOK, Oct 16 : Finance leaders of the G7 grouping agreed to hold tabletop exercises to guard against AI cyber attacks, Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said, as policymakers increasingly seek to coordinate responses to growing cyber security risks. The agreement comes after the International Monetary Fund warned this week that confidence could be undermined by an AI-enabled cyber attack on a critical service of a financial institution. Katayama's remarks to reporters on Thursday followed a meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors of the G7 advanced economies held on the sidelines of the IMF's annual gathering in Bangkok, the Thai capital. The plan will feature simulations evolved by G7 finance authorities to test how they can respond to AI-driven cyber attacks, said a Japanese finance ministry official who attended the finance leaders' meeting.

The results will test effectiveness of existing protocols and be used to revise manuals to better tackle such incidents, the official told reporters. The exercises by G7 finance ministries and central banks could include private financial institutions depending on the nature of simulations, the official added. Banking regulators globally are stepping up efforts to contain growing AI risks, Reuters reported, with some pointing to the potential for cyberattacks on banks or rogue agents undermining global financial stability. Among them is the Bank of England, which is working with banks on deep cyber-recovery options, its deputy governor said on Thursday, adding that they can no longer assume their defences are immune to AI-enabled cyberattacks.

BANGKOK, Oct 16 : World Bank President Ajay Banga on Friday said the development lender has set a goal of quintupling its critical minerals business in five years, and has identified 20 countries that it can partner with on critical minerals development projects. Banga revealed the new goal in prepared remarks to a plenary session at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. "In critical minerals, we plan to quintuple our business in five years," Banga said. "This week, we launched our first country compacts with MDB partners—to build local industries and keep more jobs and value at home." The World Bank's new Metals and Minerals implementation plan is targeting $19 billion in critical minerals financing over the fiscal 2026-2030 period, compared with $3.6 billion in the fiscal 2021-2025 period.

Critical minerals development is an area where the United States, the World Bank's largest shareholder, has called for the bank to devote more financing resources. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said earlier this week that he wanted the bank to play a bigger role in enabling critical minerals mining and processing capacity through project de-risking and finance and investment in enabling infrastructure. He said this includes deep-sea mining projects. Banga did not mention deep-sea mining, but the bank's metals plan calls for a "precautionary approach" to the nascent sector, adding that any engagement and investments must be consistent with applicable bank policies. Banga reviewed the World Bank's overall increases in financing during the 2026 fiscal year that ended on June 30, including mobilizing $112 billion in private capital, a more than threefold increase from the 2022 fiscal year, before he assumed his role. Alongside lending from the World Bank's own balance sheet, this brought the group's total financing to $230 billion for fiscal 2026, he said.

Source: Reuters

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday (Oct 15) that Washington is holding talks with Moscow and Beijing aimed at denuclearising the countries with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons. Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads, followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The US outpaces Russia in the number of deployed warheads. During an interview with Newsmax, Trump said he expects China to "catch up" with the US within the next five years. "The whole thing is a shame, because I'd love to denuclearise if possible, but we're actually talking to Russia about that, and we're talking to China about that denuclearisation," Trump told the outlet. Newsmax reported that Trump had spoken with Chinese President Xi Jinping about denuclearisation. Trump's comments come months after the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty expired earlier this year. The New START treaty signed in 2010 allowed one single extension, which was agreed by former President Joe Biden and Russian President Vladimir Putin for five years. Any new extension would require an executive decision to voluntarily extend the limits of the treaty.

FAST

WASHINGTON: New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said on Thursday (Oct 15) she did not pass the bar exam after facing scrutiny about her legal career before becoming the top spokeswoman for US President Donald Trump. Zacharia, who joined the White House on Monday, has previously said she practised law before entering politics, and Trump had described her as an attorney. "You did not pass the bar exam, correct?" she was asked in an interview on Fox News' Hannity show late on Thursday. "Correct," she said in response to the host, Sean Hannity.

"I did not," she said when Hannity asked if she ever took the bar exam a second time.

Zacharia earned her law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011, according to the university. Nearly all licensed US lawyers first obtain a law degree, but law school graduates cannot legally practice law in the US without first being admitted to a state bar. On Tuesday during her first briefing, she took questions from just three reporters before ending the event in under 15 minutes. Her performance was criticised by some media commentators and political analysts, though Trump told reporters: "I thought she was very good." When asked about her performance by Hannity, she said: "What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate to do the press conference, Sean, with very little prep time."

Source: Reuters/nh
